02 / HOW IT WORKS
Encode data through the sampler
We use the sampler to encode arbitrary data into LLM output. The model gives us probabilities for the next token. We assign each candidate a range whose size reflects its probability, then use the ciphertext to choose a token from those ranges. To recover the data, we run the same model on the output text and reconstruct those choices.

The opening sets the context
The first paragraph gives the model its starting context, so it shapes the subject, voice, and style of the generated text. It is included in the cover text so the decoder can use exactly the same context. You can write a different opening paragraph to produce a different kind of text while using the same encoding method.
Using traditional encryption
We recommend encrypting sensitive data with an established tool such as age or GPG before embedding it in cover text. This gives you a separate encryption layer with its own keys. The codec already uses authenticated encryption with a key derived from your key material and the opening paragraph, so encrypting beforehand is optional. Use the CLI for binary ciphertext and select --compression raw to skip compression.

04 / SETUP
Install and launch
Install Ollama, Python 3.10+ with venv, and Git. Then clone the project and run the launcher.
Run the launcher to install Python dependencies, download the pinned model, check replay, and open the app.
Install a compatible llama-server if your Ollama installation does not include one. Run ./run-local.sh --check to check prerequisites.
We have tested this setup on Linux. Exit the launcher to stop both servers.
TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/jchook/plaintext-to-plaintext.git
cd plaintext-to-plaintext
./run-local.sh
Manual setup and troubleshooting


      
Backend requirements
Use a backend with repeatable next-token probabilities, exact token IDs and bytes, token-history control, and reversible tokenization. Check these capabilities before using a chat-compatible endpoint.
We currently support a pinned llama-server profile with a model downloaded through Ollama. Connect to an existing compatible server with ./run-local.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:11535. Run the launcher to check model identity and replay.
Direct Ollama API support is not implemented. To add a model, define its tokenizer, prompt, and sampling rules, then verify exact recovery.
